passed.title: Expr.list.slice takes a length, not an end index
passed.trap: Python and pandas slicing habits read `slice(1, 3)` as elements 1 up to 3. In `Expr.list.slice` the second argument is `length`, the number of elements to take starting at `offset`. Writing `slice(start, stop)` silently returns `stop` elements instead of `stop - start`, with no error. Pass `length=stop - start`, or omit `length` to slice to the end of each list.
passed.example:
import polars as pl

df = pl.DataFrame({"a": [[10, 20, 30, 40, 50], [1, 2, 3, 4]]})
start, stop = 1, 3
out = df.select(
    python_habit=pl.col("a").list.slice(start, stop),
    correct=pl.col("a").list.slice(start, stop - start),
    to_end=pl.col("a").list.slice(start),
)
print(out.to_dicts())

passed.title: Expr.list.diff and Expr.list.shift restart in every sublist and leave nulls
passed.trap: `Expr.list.diff` and `Expr.list.shift` work inside each sublist independently. Nothing carries over from the previous row, so the first `n` slots of every list become null. With the default `null_behavior='ignore'`, `Expr.list.diff` keeps those nulls, and the output list has the same length as the input. Pass `null_behavior='drop'` to drop the leading nulls, which makes each list shorter by `n`. If you want differences across rows, use `Expr.diff` on a non-list column instead.
passed.example:
import polars as pl

df = pl.DataFrame({"a": [[1, 2, 4], [10, 7]]})
out = df.select(
    diff_default=pl.col("a").list.diff(),
    diff_drop=pl.col("a").list.diff(null_behavior="drop"),
    shifted=pl.col("a").list.shift(),
    lead=pl.col("a").list.shift(-1),
)
print(out.to_dicts())

passed.title: Expr.list.sample returns one element by default and is unseeded
passed.trap: When neither `n` nor `fraction` is given, `Expr.list.sample` defaults to `n=1`. It does not return a reordered copy of the whole list, so the other elements are silently lost. With `seed=None` (the default), every run draws a new random seed, so results are not reproducible. To shuffle whole lists, pass `fraction=1.0, shuffle=True`, and always set `seed` when you need deterministic output.
passed.example:
import polars as pl

df = pl.DataFrame({"v": [[1, 2, 3], [4, 5]]})
out = df.select(
    default_len=pl.col("v").list.sample(seed=0).list.len(),
    full_len=pl.col("v")
    .list.sample(fraction=1.0, shuffle=True, seed=0)
    .list.len(),
)
print(out.to_dicts())
